key_insight: In tests with inserted methodological errors, 15 LLMs detected 53%–99% of major errors, versus 27% for untrained human reviewers in an earlier experiment.
clinical_relevance: LLM-assisted review could help identify methodological problems in clinical trial reports, but these findings do not establish improved clinical outcomes.
method: Tested 15 LLMs, including four open-weight models, on three previously studied randomized trial reports.
Repeated testing on 58 randomized trials reported as published in 2026 to reduce memorization risk.
Scored 1,796 reviews using two blinded LLM judges.
evidence_signal: On the 58-trial set, reported major-error detection scores ranged from 58% to 99% overall and 66% to 89% for open-weight models.
watch_item: Models also flagged 14%–29% of error types in reports without inserted errors, raising concerns about unsupported flags and the need for expert verification.
paper_title: Large language models detect methodological errors that human peer review misses in clinical trials
